title: Latency-contingent regional throttle and safety harness for model variant failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement an automated, latency-contingent safety harness that controls regional/tier routing and triggers model-variant failovers based on correlated signals (429 spikes, p95/p99 latency growth, timeouts, and error-rate thresholds). This ticket designs and implements the routing-side circuit mechanism and the orchestration primitives used by the router to: (1) rapidly protect downstream model pools from overload, (2) attempt gentle recovery probes, and (3) provide high-fidelity telemetry and operator controls for gradual rollout. The system must support per-route, per-model-variant, and per-region configurations and be compatible with Dedicated and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Router exposes per-route circuit state (CLOSED/DEGRADED/OPEN) and reasons via the Console and traces

Automatic transition to fallback model variant or alternate region on: sustained 429 rate > configured threshold OR p99 latency > threshold OR request timeout rate > threshold within a rolling 60s window
Soft-open probing policy implemented: when a circuit moves from OPEN->DEGRADED, send controlled probes at a configurable rate and only fully close when probe success ratio >= configured threshold
Rate-limited failover to fallback variants with token-bucket to avoid stampede on recovery
Configurable sliding-window detection logic (window size and sampling granularity) available via API and Console
End-to-end e2e tests that simulate 429 floods, latency inflation, and timeout storms and assert correct state transitions and fallback behaviors
Observability: traces, per-route metrics (429_count, p95_latency, p99_latency, timeout_rate, circuit_state_changes), and a dashboard + alert runbook
Canary rollout plan documented and applied to a non-critical route before broad rollout
implementation_notes: Detection: use exponential moving average + sliding-window counters for 429s and error rates; compute p95/p99 from aggregated histograms emitted by runtime workers

Circuit states: CLOSED (normal), DEGRADED (partial routing to fallback with probes), OPEN (route fully diverted to fallback until cooldown expires), FORCED_OPEN (manual operator override), FORCED_CLOSED (operator override to bypass automation)
Transition rules: require both signal magnitude and duration to flip state (e.g., 429_rate > 0.05 AND sustained for >= 30s), configurable per-route
Probes: gradual probe ramp-up (start at 1 req/s, double every probe-interval if success rate high) with exponential backoff on failures
Failover policy: maintain per-variant weight table; when DEGRADED, shift X% of traffic to fallback variant; when OPEN shift 100%
Rate-limiter: token-bucket per-route during recovery to prevent reconnection storm; tokens refill at configured rate and cap concurrent probes
Telemetry: emit detailed events on state transitions with context (route, model_variant, region, sample request IDs) to tracing pipeline
Compatibility: config exposed in the same routing policy proto used by Dedicated/Private; maintain backwards compatible defaults
Console: build a small state inspector that shows recent transitions, current thresholds, and a manual override toggle
Testing harness: extend chaos-in-a-box to simulate worker saturation and inject synthetic 429s/timeouts; add unit tests for threshold math and simulated timeline tests for state machine
decisions: Use combined-signal logic (429s + latency + timeout) rather than single-signal triggers to reduce false positives, because spikes in one metric alone often reflect client behavior
Adopt a DEGRADED state to allow phased, reversible migration to fallback variants instead of immediate full cutover, balancing availability and output quality
Implement per-route defaults that are conservative (longer detection windows) and allow aggressive overrides for high-risk/high-priority customers
Avoid hard-coded global thresholds; prefer route-level params surfaced in Console for operator tuning
Prefer token-bucket recovery gating over simple fixed-rate probe to reduce reconnection stampede on large fleets
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-eager failovers could reduce output quality by switching away from best-accuracy variants. Mitigation: per-route quality weighting and manual override; keep fallback variants of known acceptable delta

Risk: Detection lag delays protective action during fast failures. Mitigation: allow emergency operator FORCED_OPEN and add a short path for extreme conditions (e.g., >50% 429 rate over 10s triggers immediate OPEN for critical routes)
Risk: Telemetry volume increases due to event emission. Mitigation: sample detailed events but emit aggregated metrics consistently; provide toggle to increase sampling during incident
Risk: Incompatible configs across Dedicated/Private deployments. Mitigation: ensure small, well-documented config schema and migration guide; provide backward-compatible defaults
qa_checks: Unit tests for sliding-window math and state machine transitions
Integration test against routing simulator with synthetic worker errors
Load test with canary route: verify fallback triggers at configured thresholds and that probes allow recovery
Regression tests confirming existing routing policies remain default for routes without explicit config
Console UI snapshot test for state inspector and manual override flows
